key_insight: Train an agent's skill as an external, optimizable text-state while keeping the base agent frozen, enabling systematic, optimizer-like improvement of skills under feedback.
problem_solved: Current skills are hand-crafted, generated one-shot, or undergo loosely controlled self-revision, which fails to reliably or reproducibly improve agent behavior; SkillOpt provides a disciplined text-space optimization framework that reliably improves skills.
method: Treat skills as external text/state separate from the frozen agent model, making skills the optimization target rather than model weights.
Run an iterative, controllable optimization loop: propose skill edits, evaluate with reproducible metrics, and accept updates under explicit update rules/constraints.
Maintain reproducibility and control by logging changes, using deterministic selection/evaluation criteria, and constraining updates to preserve safety and interpretability.
impact: Makes skill development for agents systematic and reproducible, allowing practitioners to reliably improve, version, and integrate agent behaviors into production workflows with optimizer-like guarantees.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen base agent block + separate 'skill' text/state that flows into agent's I/O
Iterative loop graphic: propose → evaluate → accept/reject → update (showing repeated cycles)
Performance chart: metric vs. iteration showing consistent improvement of skill over time (before/after comparison)
Icons/labels: reproducibility (checklist), controllability (sliders), and interpretability (magnifying glass over text)
paper_title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
paper_authors: Yifan Yang, Ziyang Gong, Weiquan Huang, Qihao Yang, Ziwei Zhou
